The burned book reveals fragmented words discernible: 

Waters vary in scale and distance. Those originating from mountains and flowing into the sea are named "mainstream waters." Waters diverging from others to join larger waters or the sea are called "branch waters." Mountain gullies with intermittent flow are termed "valley waters." Waters emerging from other gullies and merging into larger waters or the sea are labeled "river waters." Waters surfacing but not flowing are known as "abyssal waters." These five types of water can be harnessed for benefit or controlled by strategic barriers. However, prolonged neglect invites peril.
Comment: Water, foremost among the five hazards. Understand the distinctions of waterways and govern them according to their nature.
